subject: Enablement: model tiering & token mapping for Cardinal Health onboarding
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Enablement: model tiering & token mapping for Cardinal Health onboarding

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As we move into the CS -> Implementation handoff, I wanted to put the initial model-tiering recommendations and token mapping in one place so your engineering and infra teams can validate capacity. Attached is a short summary and a working token-estimates workbook. High-level asks below: 

- Can you confirm the single-request SLA target? (p95 latency target; you mentioned ~600ms for lookup flows)
- Are there hard constraints on context length for the patient-summary use case? We assumed 6k tokens for the first pass and 1.5k for follow-ups.
- Please flag any regulatory constraints on caching (prefix/KV cache) or retention — that will affect our recommended tiering.

Initial recommendations (see attachment "model_profiles_summary.pdf"):
1) Tier A (low-latency, high-throughput): rw-lite-8B-q4 (quantized) — for short lookups and structured extraction (<=2k context).
2) Tier B (balanced quality / cost): rw-13B-chat (q8_0) — for multi-paragraph summaries and Q&A (2k–8k context).
3) Tier C (long-context / high-quality): rw-70B-extended (fp16 / segmented KV cache) — for full patient history summarization (8k–64k windows, stream-friendly).

Token traffic estimates are in "token_estimates_v2.xlsx". Monica, Ben and Grace — please review the assumptions sheet: we used current Cardinal MAU = 12k active users, avg 3 requests/day, median input size 700 tokens, expected 30% of requests hitting long-context summarization.

Next steps:
- Elena: confirm SLA and regulatory notes by EOD Mon (22 Nov)
- Redwood: we will produce a canary deployment plan and a short ops runbook for model fallbacks and routing.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of CS Enablement | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

----

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Enablement: model tiering & token mapping for Cardinal Health onboarding

Thanks Lauren — I reviewed the traffic assumptions and made a couple of small updates to the workbook (attached). Key clarifications and conservative adjustments:

- We adjusted median input size to 900 tokens (Cardinal noted larger EHR snippets in the onboarding call).
- We modeled a 15% sampling rate of requests that escalate from Tier A -> Tier B due to follow-up context.
- For long-context summarization we split the workload into two buckets: 8k-window (70% of long requests) and 32k-window (30% of long requests). Token expansion for 32k windows uses streaming and segment recomposition; this increases per-request compute but keeps peak memory manageable.

Recommendations from ops perspective:
- Canary with Tier B (rw-13B-chat) first — provides most of the quality we need while keeping cost predictable. Route read-only lookups to Tier A where exactness is high and latency matters.
- Enable prefix caching on the 8k-window flows only (not on 32k) until we have PII-safe cache validation.
- For the 32k flows consider an offline batch summarizer as fallthrough if real-time latency constraints are strict; include that in the ramp_playbook.md.

Attachments: token_estimates_v2.xlsx (revised)

Monica Patel
Solutions Architect, Implementation | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

----

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@cardinalhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enablement: model tiering & token mapping for Cardinal Health onboarding

Team — thanks for the detail. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) SLA: internal stakeholders are targeting p95 <= 600ms for lookup flows (Tier A). For longer summarization flows p95 <= 2s is acceptable for batch-like UI actions.
2) Context constraints: legal flagged that full patient documents may contain PHI; caching is allowed only for token-level ephemeral caches with encryption at rest. No long-term retention.
3) Canary: we want a canary that starts in our staging environment and then a 2-week limited prod test with 1% of traffic. Can you include an ops play with fallback to single-model degrade (Tier B -> Tier A) and an emergency cold-start rollback?

Elena — please loop me if I missed anything. Raj will co-own the production cutover schedule.

Best,
Elena Morales
Senior Product Manager, Clinical Integrations | Cardinal Health
elena.morales@cardinalhealth.com

----

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cardinalhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2027 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Enablement: model tiering & token mapping for Cardinal Health onboarding

Good catch on the caching constraints. Quick operational notes and next actions from Redwood: 

- We'll produce the 1% traffic canary playbook (staging -> limited prod) and include automated health checks (latency, error rate, token cost delta). Draft to you by end of day Thu (25 Nov).
- Ben will own the routing policies and model-fallback configuration; Monica will author the rollback runbook sections.
- Our implementation plan will list model pins and quantization knobs per Tier so Cardinal can replicate in private deployment if needed.

Action items: 
- Elena / Raj: confirm staging credentials and the two test accounts for the 2-week limited prod window.
- Lauren: finalize the internal kickoff doc and invite the Cardinal infra leads to the rollout sync (proposed Thu 25 Nov 11am PT).

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
